q: What is the single most specific initial lab test for Rheumatoid Arthritis, and what DMARD should be started immediately upon diagnosis?
a: Anti-CCP (Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide, > 95% specificity) antibody; Methotrexate is first-line DMARD (monitor CBC, LFTs, and chest X-ray for pulmonary toxicity).

q: In a patient with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), which laboratory parameters best correlate with active lupus nephritis and overall disease flares?
a: High anti-dsDNA antibody titers combined with decreased serum complement levels (C3 and C4).

q: What is the definitive treatment for Scleroderma Renal Crisis (SRC), and which class of medications is strictly contraindicated due to triggering SRC?
a: Treatment: Immediate high-dose ACE inhibitors (e.g., captopril); Contraindication: High-dose systemic corticosteroids (precipitates/worsens SRC).

q: Patients with primary Sjögren Syndrome have a > 40-fold increased risk of developing which specific long-term systemic complication?
a: B-cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (most commonly MALT lymphoma; suspect if persistent painless parotid gland enlargement or lymphadenopathy develops).

q: How do you clinically and diagnostically distinguish Dermatomyositis from Polymyositis?
a: Dermatomyositis presents with skin manifestations (Gottron papules, heliotrope rash, shawl sign) and has a strong association with underlying occult malignancy (requires age-appropriate cancer screening). Both feature elevated CK/aldolase and proximal muscle weakness.

q: What is the immediate initial management for a patient suspected of having Giant Cell (Temporal) Arteritis with visual symptoms?
a: Immediate high-dose systemic corticosteroids (e.g., IV methylprednisolone or oral prednisone 60 mg/day) BEFORE obtaining a temporal artery biopsy to prevent irreversible blindness.

q: What is the most common extra-articular manifestation of Ankylosing Spondylitis, and what is the first-line pharmacotherapy?
a: Extra-articular: Acute anterior uveitis (unilateral painful red eye and photophobia); First-line tx: NSAIDs (e.g., indomethacin, naproxen) combined with continuous physical therapy/exercise.

q: What clinical triad defines Reactive Arthritis, and what HLA association is present in > 80% of affected patients?
a: Triad: Urethritis, Conjunctivitis, and asymmetric Oligoarthritis ("can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree"); Associated with HLA-B27 following GI (Salmonella, Shigella, Yersinia, Campylobacter) or GU (Chlamydia trachomatis) infection.

q: Which characteristic radiographic feature and physical exam findings are pathognomonic for Psoriatic Arthritis?
a: Radiography: "Pencil-in-cup" deformity of the DIP joints; Exam: Dactylitis ("sausage digits"), nail pitting, and distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint arthritis.

q: Describe the synovial fluid crystal findings in acute Gout vs. Pseudogout (CPPD) under polarized light microscopy.
a: Gout: Needle-shaped, strongly negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals (yellow when parallel to axis); Pseudogout: Rhomboid-shaped, weakly positively birefringent calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (Ca2P2O7) crystals (blue when parallel).

q: What is the first-line pharmacotherapy for Fibromyalgia, and what baseline lab abnormalities are expected?
a: First-line tx: Non-pharmacologic therapy (aerobic exercise, sleep hygiene); FDA-approved meds include Duloxetine, Pregabalin, or Milnacipran; Labs: All baseline inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP, CK) and labs are completely normal.

q: A patient presents with chronic recurrent sinusitis, cavitary lung nodules with hemoptysis, and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. What is the diagnosis and target autoantibody?
a: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA / Wegener's); Associated with PR3-ANCA / c-ANCA (anti-proteinase 3).

q: What clinical features and lab finding differentiate Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (EGPA) from Microscopic Polyangiitis (MPA)?
a: EGPA presents with severe refractory asthma, allergic rhinitis/nasal polyps, and peripheral eosinophilia (> 10%); Associated with MPO-ANCA / p-ANCA.

q: Polyarteritis Nodosa (PAN) characteristically affects medium-sized arteries. Which organ system is classically spared, and which viral infection is strongly associated?
a: Lungs are classically spared (no pulmonary involvement); Strongly associated with chronic Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) (and Hepatitis C) infection.

q: What is the classic clinical tetrad of IgA Vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein Purpura)?
a: Tetrad: Palpable purpura (buttocks/lower extremities without thrombocytopenia), Arthralgias, Abdominal pain (risk of intussusception), and Renal disease (IgA mesangial deposition).

q: What is the diagnostic hallmark autoantibody for Mixed Connective Tissue Disease (MCTD), and what three diseases overlap in MCTD?
a: Antibody: Anti-U1 RNP (ribonucleoprotein); Overlap features of: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), Systemic Sclerosis, and Polymyositis.

q: What autoantibodies and coagulation lab finding are characteristic of Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APLS)?
a: Autoantibodies: Anti-β2-glycoprotein I, Anti-cardiolipin, and Lupus Anticoagulant; Lab finding: Paradoxically prolonged aPTT that fails to correct on a 1:1 mixing study.

q: What synovial fluid white blood cell (WBC) count threshold confirms Septic Arthritis, and what is the empiric antibiotic coverage for a native joint?
a: Synovial fluid WBC: > 50,000/mm3 with > 75-90% PMNs; Empiric tx: IV Vancomycin (covers MRSA) plus 3rd generation cephalosporin (e.g., Ceftriaxone, covers Gram-negative rods/Neisseria).

q: What is the classic symptom triad of Behçet Disease, and what office test supports the diagnosis?
a: Triad: Recurrent painful oral aphthous ulcers, genital ulcers, and uveitis; Positive Pathergy test (sterile pustule forms 24-48 hours after needle prick).

q: How do you clinically differentiate Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR) from Polymyositis regarding muscle strength and muscle enzymes?
a: PMR presents with proximal muscle stiffness/pain with NORMAL muscle strength and NORMAL muscle enzymes (CK, aldolase) but markedly elevated ESR/CRP; Polymyositis presents with TRUE proximal muscle weakness and ELEVATED muscle enzymes (CK/aldolase).
